arxiv-1609-08571.creator: Johannes Bausch, Elizabeth Crosson
arxiv-1609-08571.description: Abstract Feynman’s circuit-to-Hamiltonian construction connects quantum computation and ground states of many-body quantum systems. Kitaev applied this construction to demonstrate QMA-completeness of the local Hamiltonian problem, and Aharanov et al. used it to show the equivalence of adiabatic computation and the quantum circuit model.

arxiv-2206-00010.title: DYNAMICAL POPULATION OF COMET RESERVOIRS
arxiv-2206-00010.creator: N. A. Kaib, Kathryn Volk
arxiv-2206-00010.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by N. A. Kaib, Kathryn Volk. The Oort cloud and the scattered disk are the two primary reservoirs for long-period and short-period comets, respectively. In this review, we assess the known observational constraints on these reservoirs’ properties and their formation. In addition, we discuss how the early orbital evolution of the giant planets generated the modern scattered disk from the early, massive planetesimal disk and how ∼ \sim 5% of this material was captured into the Oort cloud.

arxiv-2310-07598.title: A Survey of Learning with Imbalanced Data, Representation Learning and SEP Forecasting Josias Moukpe Florida Institute of Technology Department of Computer Science and Engineering
arxiv-2310-07598.description: Abstract Deep Learning methods have significantly advanced various data-driven tasks such as regression, classification, and forecasting. However, much of this progress has been predicated on the strong but often unrealistic assumption that training datasets are balanced with respect to the targets they contain.

arxiv-2311-07744.title: Two-Stage Aggregation with Dynamic Local Attention for Irregular Time Series
arxiv-2311-07744.creator: Xiaochen Zheng, Xingyu Chen, Amina Mollaysa, Manuel Schürch, Ahmed Allam, Michael Krauthammer
arxiv-2311-07744.description: Abstract Irregular multivariate time series data is characterized by varying time intervals between consecutive observations of measured variables/signals (i.e., features) and varying sampling rates (i.e., recordings/measurement) across these features. Modeling time series while taking into account these irregularities is still a challenging task for machine learning methods.

arxiv-2504-12931.title: Explainable AI in Usable Privacy and Security: Challenges and Opportunities
arxiv-2504-12931.creator: Vincent Freiberger, Arthur Fleig, Erik Buchmann
arxiv-2504-12931.description: Abstract . Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly being used for automated evaluations and explaining them. However, concerns about explanation quality, consistency, and hallucinations remain open research challenges, particularly in high-stakes contexts like privacy and security, where user trust and decision-making are at stake.

arxiv-2506-05528.title: Combinatorics of descent algebras and graph coverings Thanks: This research was supported by the project CARPLO, ANR-20-CE40-0007.
arxiv-2506-05528.creator: Philippe Biane
arxiv-2506-05528.description: Abstract . We give a direct combinatorial proof that the product of two descent classes in a symmetric group is a sum of descent classes. The proof is based on the fact that the group product gives a covering map when descent classes are endowed with the graph structure coming from the weak order.

arxiv-2506-15455.title: Re-Imagine : Symbolic Benchmark Synthesis for Reasoning Evaluation
arxiv-2506-15455.creator: Xinnuo Xu, Rachel Lawrence, Kshitij Dubey, Atharva Pandey, Risa Ueno, Fabian Falck, Aditya V. Nori, Rahul Sharma, Amit Sharma, Javier Gonzalez

Nori, Rahul Sharma, Amit Sharma, Javier Gonzalez. Recent Large Language Models (LLMs) have reported high accuracy on reasoning benchmarks. However, it is still unclear whether the observed results arise from true “reasoning” or from statistical recall of the training set.

arxiv-2507-18105.title: Understanding the Supply Chain and Risks of Large Language Model Applications
arxiv-2507-18105.creator: Yujie Ma, Lili Quan, Xiaofei Xie, Qiang Hu, Jiongchi Yu, Yao Zhang, Sen Chen
arxiv-2507-18105.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) have seen rapid development, leading to the widespread deployment of LLM-based systems across various domains. As these systems become increasingly applied into real-world scenarios, understanding the potential risks associated with their complex ecosystems is of growing importance.

arxiv-2510-21273.title: Enforcing Calibration in Multi-Output Probabilistic Regression with Pre-rank Regularization
arxiv-2510-21273.creator: Naomi Desobry, Elnura Zhalieva, Souhaib Ben Taieb
arxiv-2510-21273.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Naomi Desobry, Elnura Zhalieva, Souhaib Ben Taieb. Probabilistic models must be well calibrated to support reliable decision-making. While calibration in single-output regression is well studied, defining and achieving multivariate calibration in multi-output regression remains considerably more challenging. The existing literature on multivariate calibration primarily focuses on diagnostic tools based on pre-rank functions, which are projections that reduce multivariate prediction-observation pairs to univariate summaries to detect specific types of miscalibration.

pmc-10647400.description: Adolescents are an at-risk group for circadian misalignment. The contribution of sleep–wake rhythm instability to the psychoemotional, cognitive, and weight disorders of adolescents has been studied in sufficient detail. At the same time, there is insufficient information about the association between chrononutrition indices and the well-being of adolescents.

pmc-11446822.title: Predicting visual function by interpreting a neuronal wiring diagram
pmc-11446822.creator: H. Sebastian Seung
pmc-11446822.description: As connectomics advances, it will become commonplace to know far more about the structure of a nervous system than about its function. The starting point for many investigations will become neuronal wiring diagrams, which will be interpreted to make theoretical predictions about function.

pmc-12534489.title: A feasibility study evaluating the usability and acceptability of the personalised space technology exercise platform mobile application
pmc-12534489.creator: Hannah M Worboys, Laura J Gray, Sarah Anthony, Rachel Hobson, Tim Lucas, Joshua D Vande Hey, Marios Panagi, G André Ng
pmc-12534489.description: The P-STEP (Personalised Space Technology Exercise Platform) app is designed to bring together tailored exercise guidance and up-to-date air quality information for individuals with long term health conditions. The app allows individuals to plan outdoor exercise walking routes while minimising their exposure to air pollution.

pmc-12539666.title: Maternal Anemia and Offspring Outcomes in India: A Scoping Review
pmc-12539666.creator: Melissa T. Benavente, Nophar Geifman, Sarah Bath, Anand Ahankari
pmc-12539666.description: BackgroundAnemia is a global burden, with women and children being most at risk. Moreover, anemia during pregnancy has been reported to be associated with adverse outcomes for both the mother and the offspring. In India, anemia is considered a national health issue and is estimated to have the highest prevalence in the world.

pmc-12730018.title: Religious and Spiritual Dimensions of Pro-Ana Discourse on X: A Linguistic Analysis for Counseling Practice
pmc-12730018.creator: Krisy Elrod, Angeliki Trifonopoulos, Martin Drapeau
pmc-12730018.description: Anorexia nervosa is among the most lethal psychiatric conditions. Online pro-anorexia (“pro-ana”) communities may frame starvation and restriction in moral or spiritual terms. This study explored how pro-ana discourse on X (formerly Twitter) encodes values, spirituality, and identity through language, with attention to clinical practice.

pmc-13552996.title: Another host, another mystery: Infection of polychaete Pista palmata (Annelida: Terebellidae) with a new blood fluke (Digenea: Aporocotylidae) in the coastal Northwest Atlantic Ocean
pmc-13552996.creator: Anna N Chowansky, Kristina M Hill-Spanik, Dennis E Kyle, Isaure de Buron
pmc-13552996.description: Terebelliform annelids can serve as intermediate hosts for blood flukes of marine fishes and sea turtles. The scarcity of global reports on the life cycles of these parasites reflects the need for further exploration. Our objective was to further our knowledge of the diversity and life cycles of blood flukes in coastal South Carolina (SC), United States.

pmc-13616197.title: Mapping Layers of Sustainability Consciousness in Food Consumption Using the Item Response Theory (IRT) Approach
pmc-13616197.creator: Zoltán Bakucs, Lajos Baráth, Zsófia Benedek, Imre Fertő, László Sipos
pmc-13616197.description: Understanding how consumers commit to sustainability in their food choices requires attention to both widely shared values and the points where commitments differ. Drawing on Item Response Theory (IRT), this study examines survey data from more than one thousand consumers to map a continuum of sustainability consciousness.

pmc-13621784.title: Post-pandemic trends in youth sport: structural and social determinants of girls’ and women's engagement in Ultimate
pmc-13621784.creator: Sarah Stokowski, Chris Corr, Andrew Rudd
pmc-13621784.description: IntroductionThe COVID-19 pandemic disrupted youth sport participation in the United States, with evidence suggesting uneven recovery and persistent gender disparities. This study examined patterns of women's and girls' engagement in Ultimate (commonly referred to as ultimate frisbee) from 2014 to 2024, considering structural and cultural contexts.

pmc-13627016.title: Consensus statement on the management of Achondroplasia in the Middle East
pmc-13627016.creator: Nandu Thalange, Tawfeg Ben Omran, Afaf Alsagheir, Khalid Hussain, Maha Faden, Mona Aglan, Sareea Alremeithi, Abdelhadi Habeb
pmc-13627016.description: Achondroplasia is the most common skeletal dysplasia and presents as a lifelong, multi-system condition characterized by disproportionate short stature, rhizomelic limb shortening, macrocephaly with frontal bossing, and a spectrum of neurological, respiratory, orthopedic, and psychosocial complications. Effective management requires anticipatory surveillance, coordinated multidisciplinary care, and early recognition of life-threatening complications.

(a) Panama Canal management, operation, and maintenance The Commission may manage, operate, and maintain the Panama Canal. (b) Establishment, maintenance, and operation of activities, facilities, and appurtenances The Commission may construct or acquire, establish.
